phase3_findings.description: src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py line 84 (new Ambiguous Questions bullet) justifies overriding the one-row rule 'because a lookup's rows are already shown above the question', which is not always true: the same prompt says at line 68 that a very large row's values may not be shown and at line 131 that such a row shows at most its column headers; _format.py also hides introspection DataFrames and trims trailing blocks to a byte budget. Criterion 5 asks for this reason nearly word for word.

docs/external/getting-started.md line 82 says the agent asks when 'the readings give different numbers' and not when 'the readings give the same numbers'; the prompt's test is whether readings count different records, a different period or a different measure, without first measuring the difference (default.py lines 80 and 83), so two readings that count different records but give the same total still get a question.

Test comments name the issue rather than the protected behavior: the banner 'clarifying questions (issue #298)' at tests/unit/test_server.py line 593 and the docstring of test_ambiguous_questions_section_always_present in tests/unit/test_system_prompt.py beginning 'Issue #298: ...'.

docs/external/managing-memory.md lines 38, 40 and 42 state instructed model behavior as certain ('then gets a clarifying question', 'it uses the reading that the pair's SQL uses', 'and then it asks'), while only a system-prompt instruction backs it and nothing enforces it; line 36 and getting-started.md hedge correctly ('is instructed to', 'is meant to').
